subject: [Urgent] FinExCo p99 latency spike — possible GPU OOM/fragmentation
content:

Attached is a sample trace from one of the timed-out requests. Can you confirm whether this looks like the same OOM issue you patched last month?

Thanks,
Grace

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API p99 regressions this morning (FinExCo)

All — I pulled the platform traces for the hosted cluster that serves FinExCo. We're seeing intermittent memory allocations that are not freed across long-running worker processes; pattern lines up with recent GPU fragmentation reports.

What I've done so far:
- Pulled GPU and host metrics for the time window (attached small extracts).
- Triggered an automated restart of the affected worker pool (vpool-15) at 09:40 PT; that brought p95 down but p99 persisted for a short tail.

Next steps (immediate):
1) David to collect full heapdump and kernel logs (David: can you prioritize?)
2) Marissa to verify model variant/quantization changes rolled in the last 72 hours (Marissa: did we push any candidate changes?)
3) Sean to throttle/route at the gateway as a temporary mitigation to remove tail latency for synchronous calls.

If p99 doesn't drop within the hour, we should consider canary rollback to previous model build and involve product execs.

- Laura
Director, Platform Reliability

-----
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API p99 regressions this morning (FinExCo)

I collected the full logs and a heap dump from the GPU process (attached: oom-dump-20260513.tar.gz). Early look: several CUDA allocations failed followed by fragmentation warnings in the runtime allocator. There are ~6 partial OOM events in the 08:38–08:46 window, which map to the timed-out requests Grace sent.

Hypothesis: a combination of a slightly larger payload distribution from FinExCo's requests plus a recent quantization tweak (smaller memory rounding) is increasing allocation pressure on long-lived inference workers, causing fragmentation that surfaces as p99 tail latency and transient errors.

Immediate mitigations I recommend:
- Rollback the quantization tweak on vpool-15 to the prior artifact (safe, fast).
- Apply a rolling restart to worker nodes with a short warm-up to flush fragmented allocations.
- Gate the largest payload paths with lighter-weight model routing for synchronous calls.

I'll open INF-4721 with exact stack traces and link to S3.

-David
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: oom-dump-20260513.tar.gz (log bundle)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API p99 regressions this morning (FinExCo)

Rishi/Team — I confirmed we deployed a micro-quant change 36 hours ago to reduce token memory for medium-length sequences; change was low-risk but could increase fragmentation in edge cases. I will prepare an immediate rollback for vpool-15, target 11:00 PT.

Also flagging that this customer uses a higher proportion of long-context requests; routing them to a fresh worker variant with aggressive prefix caching should reduce allocation churn.

-Marissa
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: API p99 regressions this morning (FinExCo)

Deployed route gating at 10:40 PT (temporary) for sync endpoints: ~15% of traffic rerouted to lower-memory model; p99 immediately improved for the majority of requests, but a tail remained for a subset of large requests. I've left the gating in place and am monitoring.

Metrics snapshot: p95 back to normal; p99 dropped from ~1.2s to ~420ms for most traffic; error rate back to baseline.

-Sean
Platform Ops

Subject: Re: API p99 regressions this morning (FinExCo)

Grace — apologies for the delayed consolidated note; below is a short executive summary you can share.

Executive Summary (for FinExCo leadership):
- Impact: On 2026-05-13 08:38–08:46 PT FinExCo observed p99 latency spikes and transient timeouts affecting a small subset (0.8%) of synchronous requests. Throughput overall was maintained; downstream retries caused temporary pipeline backlog.
- Root cause (current working hypothesis): GPU memory fragmentation in the hosted inference pool serving FinExCo (vpool-15) aggravated by a recent low-risk quantization tweak and an atypical distribution of large-context payloads from FinExCo during the window. Fragmentation led to transient allocation failures (partial OOMs) and tail latency.
- Immediate actions taken (May 13):
  1) Automated restart of affected worker pool (09:40 PT) to clear fragmentation.
  2) Temporary routing/gating of largest synchronous requests to a lower-memory variant (deployed 10:40 PT) — measurable p99 improvement.
  3) Collected heap dumps and logs (oom-dump-20260513.tar.gz) and opened INF-4721 for detailed trace analysis.
- Near-term remediation (next 72 hours):
  1) Rollback the recent quantization tweak for vpool-15 (planned 11:00 PT on May 13; completed successfully).
  2) Rolling restart across the affected fleet to reduce fragmentation risk.
  3) Implement routing policy for long-context requests to stabilized worker variants and increase KV/prefix caching for their workload.
  4) Engineering follow-up: optimize allocator behavior for mixed payload distributions and add proactive fragmentation detection to the console alerts.
- Customer-facing mitigations: We will provide a post-mortem doc, share the INF-4721 ticket with trace links, and set up a short architecture call to agree on routing/SLAs.

Attachments/links: INF-4721 (JIRA), s3://redwood-logs/finexco/oom-20260513/heapdump.tar.gz, p99-trace-heap-20260513.pdf

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow with our SRE and product leads to walk your CTO through the technical details and the 72-hour plan.

Thanks — we appreciate the flag and will follow through.

Rishi Malhotra
